title: Preserving Crop Products
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Sun-dry thin slices of mango, sukuma wiki or tomatoes on a clean raised rack covered with a net. Knives are used by the teacher or with a teacher holding the board.

skills.key_step: The child says how crop produce is preserved at home by drying (cut thin, dried on a clean raised rack in the sun, stored dry and sealed) and why dry food keeps (germs and moulds need water to grow).

floor.prerequisite: Knows how grain is dried and stored.
floor.question: Why must grain be dry before storing?
floor.answer: so it does not go mouldy

steps: Dry on a clean raised rack in the sun.
contexts: dried sukuma wiki for the dry season

board.do: Write "why does dried mango keep for months?".

misconceptions.ask: When may dried maize be stored?
misconceptions.repair: Store one damp and one dry sample and see which grows mould.

listen_for: On the floor in an open sack
misconceptions.ask: Where should dry produce be stored?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a sack on the floor and one on a pallet.

listen_for: The sun makes it harmless for ever
misconceptions.ask: Why does dry food keep longer?
misconceptions.repair: Add water to dried food and watch it spoil.

misconceptions.ask: Why are mangoes cut into thin slices for drying?
misconceptions.repair: Dry a thick and a thin slice side by side for two days.

checks.question: Why does dried food keep longer?
checks.answer: moulds and germs need water to grow

checks.question: Name a fruit that can be sun-dried.

skills.key_step: The child orders the steps of sun-drying (choose fresh, wash, cut thin and even, spread on a raised rack, cover with a net, turn, take in at night, dry until crisp or leathery, cool and store sealed) and tells when it is dry.
steps: Spread on a raised rack; cover.

board.do: Write the cards: store, cut thin, dry on a rack.
Order them: cut thin, dry, store.

misconceptions.ask: Where should vegetables be spread for drying?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what reaches food on the ground: dust, chickens, insects.

misconceptions.ask: Why are slices for drying cut the same thickness?
misconceptions.repair: Dry a thick and a thin slice on the same tray and feel both after a day.

misconceptions.ask: What should be done with drying produce in the evening?
misconceptions.repair: Touch a slice left out overnight: it is damp again.

listen_for: It has been in the sun one day
misconceptions.ask: How do you know dried sukuma wiki is ready to store?
misconceptions.repair: Break a crisp and a limp leaf.

checks.question: Why cover drying produce with a net?
checks.answer: to keep off flies, dust and birds

checks.question: How do you know dried mango is ready?
checks.answer: it is leathery, not sticky or wet
